result.executive_summary: Q3 FY2026 showed strong growth, led by record data-center revenue, while sequential gross-margin pressure and expected export-license impacts temper the outlook. Management expects Q4 revenue of $4.0–$4.2 billion and gross margin of approximately 60%, and described its guidance as cautious given uncertainty around licenses and supply reallocation. result.what_happened: The results release reports Q3 FY2026 revenue of $4.2 billion, up 31% year over year and 6% sequentially. Data-center revenue reached a record $2.94 billion, up 44% year over year. Gross margin was 61.5%, down 1.2 percentage points sequentially amid higher packaging costs; operating income was $1.3 billion and diluted EPS was $1.12. On the call, management said Q4 revenue is expected to be $4.0–$4.2 billion and gross margin approximately 60%. It estimated that new export-license requirements will reduce Q4 revenue by $300 million, said it is discussing supply reallocation, and cautioned that the duration and outcome remain unclear. The release also reports $5.8 billion in cash, $2.1 billion in long-term debt, and approval of a $1.0 billion share repurchase program.

transcript_preview.speaker: Operator
transcript_preview.text: Good afternoon, and welcome to the Northwind Semiconductors third quarter fiscal 2026 earnings call. Today's call contains forward-looking statements, and actual results may differ materially. I will now hand the call over to our Chief Executive Officer, Dana Reyes.

transcript_preview.speaker: Dana Reyes
transcript_preview.text: Thank you, and good afternoon, everyone. Northwind delivered record revenue of $4.2 billion this quarter, up 31% from a year ago, driven by demand for our data center accelerators. Data center revenue grew 44%, and now represents 70% of our business. At the same time, I want to be transparent about two headwinds. First, new export license requirements for advanced chips shipping to certain regions will reduce our fourth quarter revenue by an estimated $300 million. Second, our largest cloud customer accounted for 22% of revenue, so our concentration remains high.

transcript_preview.speaker: Speaker 1
transcript_preview.text: Thanks, Dana. Gross margin was 61.5%, down 1.2 points sequentially, mainly because of higher packaging costs. Operating income was $1.3 billion. We ended the quarter with $5.8 billion in cash and $2.1 billion of long-term debt. For the fourth quarter, we expect revenue of $4.0 to $4.2 billion, which includes the impact of the export restrictions, and gross margin of approximately 60%. We are also announcing a new $1 billion share repurchase program.

transcript_preview.speaker: Priya
transcript_preview.text: Thanks for taking my question. Can you quantify how much of the guidance reduction is temporary, and whether you can redirect that supply to other customers?

transcript_preview.speaker: Dana Reyes
transcript_preview.text: Great question, Priya. We believe part of the impact is temporary while licenses are reviewed, and we are already in conversations to reallocate supply. However, we are being cautious in our guidance until we have more clarity.

transcript_preview.speaker: Operator
transcript_preview.text: That concludes today's question-and-answer session. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
